# Legacy (Tauri v0.1) data fixtures

These files were **produced from the format specification, not by the old Rust binary** (there is no Rust
toolchain in this environment). They are generated by the C# re-implementation in
`tests/MySSH.Storage.Tests/LegacyFormat.cs` from the definitions in `tests/MySSH.Storage.Tests/Fixtures.cs`,
following `tools/legacy/storage.rs.txt` and `tools/legacy/models.rs.txt`:

| File | Format |
|---|---|
| `appdata/myssh/.key` | 32 raw bytes (AES-256 key). Fixed test value: SHA-256 of a constant string. **Not a secret.** |
| `appdata/myssh/servers.json` | `serde_json::to_string_pretty(HashMap<String, EncryptedServerConfig>)`: 2-space indent, struct field order, raw UTF-8, no trailing newline. Secret fields are `base64(nonce(12) ‖ AES-256-GCM ciphertext ‖ tag(16))` with the `.key`, no AAD. |
| `backup-v1.txt` | Legacy export: `base64(0x01 ‖ nonce(12) ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag(16))`, key = `SHA-256(UTF-8(password) ‖ "myssh-export-salt-v1")`, plaintext = compact JSON array of plain `ServerConfig`. Password: `fixture-backup-password`. |

Nonces are derived deterministically (SHA-256 of a seed and a counter) so the files can be regenerated byte for
byte; `FixtureGenerationTests` fails if the committed files drift from the generator. To regenerate:

```sh
MYSSH_REGENERATE_FIXTURES=1 dotnet test tests/MySSH.Storage.Tests
```

## Contents of `servers.json`

| id prefix | case |
|---|---|
| `1111…` Bastion | password auth (`root` / `hunter2`) |
| `2222…` 生产服务器 🚀 本番 | unicode name + notes, port 2222, same `root` / `hunter2` as Bastion (password identity dedupe) |
| `3333…` | private key **with** passphrase, SOCKS5 proxy with username + password |
| `4444…` | private key **without** passphrase, HTTP proxy without credentials |
| `5555…` / `6666…` | two hosts sharing the same private key (key identity dedupe); `6666…` uses the same SOCKS5 proxy as `3333…` (proxy dedupe) |
| `7777…` | `jump_host` = Bastion (→ `JumpChain`) |
| `8888…` | corrupted record: one byte of the password ciphertext flipped (must be reported and skipped, not fatal) |

`backup-v1.txt` holds three servers: a password host, a key host (passphrase, HTTP proxy with credentials, Cyrillic
name) and a host using the first one as `jump_host`.

The private "keys" are placeholder text (`-----BEGIN TEST KEY-----`), not real key material.
